output.summary: A tall herbaceous perennial of unstated native origin, giant fennel has hollow stalks and produces resin from its root or lower stalk. Its young stems and flower clusters were eaten in ancient Rome and remain eaten in Morocco, though culinary use can cause poisoning.
output.edibilityNote: Young stems and inflorescences were eaten in ancient Rome and remain eaten in Morocco; poisoning can occur, and Sardinia has poisonous and non-poisonous chemotypes.
